hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained as Florida Forest Service warns of more to come this summer
hero.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said the department is in peak fire season. The summer heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them receptive to ignition when lightning strikes occur. Rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later.

The Florida Forest Service says the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon, but residents should not be alarmed. Grubitch explained that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire.

Grubitch stressed that the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. If you see something, say something, he said, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: TCCEED summer internship program places 61 Treasure Coast students in paid local jobs
cards.teaser: The second-year TCCEED summer internship program doubled employer participation and placed 61 students in paid positions across the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
The TCCEED summer internship program doubled employer participation in its second year and placed 61 students in paid local jobs. The program also tripled the number of applications from Treasure Coast students compared to the previous year.

The initiative provides paid work experience for local students with Treasure Coast businesses. The expanded participation demonstrates growing interest from both employers and students in the region.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner defeats Alexander Zverev to win second consecutive Wimbledon title
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his second consecutive Wimbledon title and fifth Grand Slam championship.
cards.body:
Sinner's victory came after his German opponent appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip on the grass at a key point in the third set. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, he dropped to the grass on his back in celebration. Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller.

The match turned at 3-3 in the third set when Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up. Zverev quickly resumed playing but appeared slightly hampered and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third when he missed a forehand.

The title was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Sinner's championship came in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open, where he wilted in a Paris heat wave. Despite the defeat, Zverev will move into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday, leapfrogging Carlos Alcaraz, who missed both the French Open and Wimbledon this year due to a right wrist injury.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's 6,000-seat soccer stadium to break ground in November at Walton & One development
cards.teaser: Professional soccer club Port St. Lucie SC released new stadium renderings and announced November groundbreaking for a 6,000-seat venue at Walton & One on U.S. 1 and Walton Road.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat soccer stadium at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Representatives announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November. While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club said the venue will be a year-round gathering place with flexibility to grow in capacity. Ticket deposits are currently available online.

Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said he thinks there is nothing to do in PSL for the most part and believes this may be the first cool thing the city has ever brought. Focus Sanders, a barber at Sapp's Barbershop, said the stadium offers more business because it will bring more people to the area, including visitors from out of town who may need haircuts. Woods said you can't really even get out on U.S. 1 before this because it's a nightmare, and the additional traffic on game days will be huge. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. Port St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements last October.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova recovers from five blown match points to win Wimbledon women's title
cards.teaser: 21-year-old Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
The 21-year-old Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. She became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance.

Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club, looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with panoramic ocean views
cards.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
cards.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years since its construction in 1860. The red brick tower stands above the inlet, and visitors can make the 105-step climb to the top via a narrow spiral staircase. Lighthouse keepers once climbed these same stairs night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners.

From the gallery at the top, panoramic views show the Atlantic Ocean stretching to the east while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel and the sea breeze provides relief from the warm Florida weather. The museum grounds feature restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's past, from its construction before the Civil War to its years as an active Coast Guard station.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
hero.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club
hero.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. "I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said.

The recognition as a flag bearer comes after his selection as Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region, one of the highest honors given by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America. As one of only 12 club members chosen nationally for this role, Rosario Liz will represent not only his local club in St. Lucie County but also youth organizations across the country at the World Cup finals. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said. He closed with a message for younger members at the club. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said.

The announcement marks a significant milestone for the Port St. Lucie teen as he prepares to transition to college life at the University of Florida while taking on this prestigious international role at the World Cup finals.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance work continues on several major roadways. The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions, with additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on drivers.

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from 8 p.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16. Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road for roadway construction. The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will also be closed from 8 p.m. Sunday through Thursday for paving and lighting installation. Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue. Weather-related contingency dates for both closures are scheduled for July 19-23.

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project, beginning at 7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continuing until 5 p.m. Portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time and access to homes and businesses will be maintained. Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads depending on the closure location. Additional lane closures are planned on SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road during daytime hours Monday through Friday, with two lanes potentially closing overnight for drainage work, milling and repaving.

Motorists should also expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line, with up to two lanes closing in each direction for milling, resurfacing and signage work. The existing A1A North Causeway drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Friday as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge, though vehicle traffic on the new bridge will not be affected. Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions, and motorists should allow additional travel time and use caution around workers and equipment.
